idiom_name: sttp client + effect-system or Future retry with a java.util.UUID operation id
implementation_notes: Retry lives in the effect layer: sttp's resilience guidance wires retries (alongside circuit breaking and rate limiting) into the request/backend stack, and with ZIO or cats-effect the attempt policy is a Schedule/retry combinator applied to the effect that sends the request. The idempotency key itself is plain JVM - java.util.UUID.randomUUID() bound to the logical operation before the effect is described and carried as a header - so every replay sends the same value. Where the code is Future-based, retries are hand-written recursion over Future.recoverWith, which makes it even easier to reuse one request value instead of rebuilding it with a fresh key.
pitfalls: Effect-system retry combinators re-run the effect, so a UUID.randomUUID() evaluated inside it is a new key per attempt; bind the key outside the retry.
Rebuilding the request inside the retry loop (a new sttp request value with a fresh .header call) is easy to write by accident and reintroduces the duplicate.
Awaiting a failed Future tells you the call failed, not whether the server committed; without a stable key, retrying that failure is a bet.
